wall_minutes_superseded.why_superseded: 4.64 belonged to the superseded 67,826-cell refinement-2 run, the same defective solve the previous_credential entry below records. Every other number on this record was re-derived from the repair ladder on 2026-07-27 and this field was not, so the credentials surface captioned the graded drag with the wall time of the run that drag replaced. It was caught on 2026-08-01 while re-pricing a proposal that had been costed from it; the proposal was corrected first and the record second.
wall_minutes_superseded.why_it_matters: the cheap number came from the defective solve, and it was cheap BECAUSE the solve was defective: 67,826 cells with addLayers false at Re 1e6, against 645,251 cells with resolved layers on the rung that replaced it. A repair priced from the wall time of the run it repairs is understated by construction, which is now a charter clause.

previous_credential.why_superseded: reference (0.03) was hand-set with no derivation script; the 67,826-cell mesh behind the 0.02892 measurement had addLayers false at Re 1e6 (no boundary-layer cells) and archived no polyMesh (not reproducible). See models/curriculum/naca4412_wing/reference.yaml notes and sdk/scripts/derive_naca4412_reference.py.

grid_study.note: 3-rung ladder, all with resolved boundary layers (add_layers=True, target y+ 30), sdk/scripts/naca4412_credential_repair.py. Cd and Cl were NOT monotonic: medium->fine Cd fell 25% (0.024478->0.018262), fine->finer Cd moved <1% (0.018262->0.018327) but Cl swung back up 19% (0.209547->0.250179). No Richardson/observed-order fit performed on non-asymptotic data. The finer (1,849,113-cell) rung independently failed the lab's own mesh non-orthogonality gate (74.96 deg, gate 70 deg) and achieved only 58.3% of its target boundary-layer thickness (vs ~94% on the other two rungs) -- degraded, not improved, at the largest cell count -- the leading suspect for the non-monotonicity. The graded rung (fine, 645,251 cells) is the only one passing both mesh gates with full layer coverage.
